title: Exact-degree Fourier estimator output
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ assign a sign in $\{-1,1\\}$ to each point of the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube. For each set of coordinates of size at most $k$, provide the prescribed number of cube inputs, and form their labels by evaluating $f$ on those inputs. The estimator returns a sparse Fourier hypothesis supported on the sets of coordinates of size at most $k$, with each coefficient obtained by rounding the empirical Fourier coefficient from its supplied inputs to the degree-$k$ Fourier granularity.
hypotheses_covered: a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
one supplied cube input for each low-degree coordinate set and sample index
